$comment: The two Metadata blocks' anatomy, case by case: the stored node in, the exact markup out.
Hand-authored and read by BOTH renderers' suites — the React `view`s
(bundle-src/test/metadata-anatomy.test.tsx) and the Chameleon templates
(src/.../tests/test_view_metadata_block_view.py and
test_view_metadata_section_block_view.py). The two renderers must emit the
same anatomy element for element, because one scope-wrapped stylesheet
dresses both surfaces; this file is what holds them to a FIXED list rather
than to whichever renderer landed first.
`html` is the markup INSIDE the host's block wrapper, on the PUBLIC surface.
The wrapper's own `block block-metadata has--block-width--<w>` stamp is the
host's and is not our output.
No whitespace between elements: the Plate editable computes
`white-space: pre-wrap`, so an inter-element newline becomes a real line box.
JSX drops it by construction; the server templates strip their indentation.
Rich text is the exception: its own whitespace is authored and kept.
Both suites compare EXACTLY, up to attribute order and the void-element
slash (each sorts attributes and drops `/>` before comparing), and again
as the SKELETON — every attribute but `class` removed, text kept — which is
the cross-renderer contract.
The editor surface is `html` with every `href` dropped (the canvas-safety
rule), and nothing else changed. An `img` keeps its `src`: it navigates
nowhere.
`catalog` in `data` is the DERIVED key the server's serializer injects: every
offered field of the content item as an `{id, title, kind, value}` row. A
node without one is a node the server has never serialized, and both
renderers draw the empty root.

metadata.name: empty
metadata.note: Exactly one element: the root. Nothing stored, nothing derived, no modifier.

metadata.name: field-without-catalog
metadata.note: A field chosen on a node the server has never serialized: the root still carries the stored field, so the author can recognise the block, and nothing else renders.

metadata.name: field-without-catalog-placeholder
metadata.note: The placeholder is the author's own content: it renders whenever a field is stored and there is no value to show, catalog or not.
metadata.html: No summary yet

metadata.name: text
metadata.note: The reference case: a text field with a value, no label asked for. The root carries the field AND its kind.
metadata.html: A short summary.

metadata.name: text-with-label
metadata.note: The label is the catalog's field title, before the value, only when the author asked for it.

metadata.name: field-missing-from-catalog
metadata.note: A stored field the catalog does not know — a hand-authored node, a field of another type — keeps its modifier and shows nothing; the label needs a title the node does not have.

metadata.name: unscreened-link-dropped
metadata.note: The catalog travels inside a JSON node anyone with API access can hand-author, so a URL is screened like typed input: a scheme outside the allowlist is treated exactly as no link.
metadata.html: • B

metadata.name: unscreened-image-dropped
metadata.note: Symmetric for images: an unscreened src is no image, and the placeholder takes its place.
metadata.html: No image

metadata.name: unsafe-field-id-gets-no-modifier
metadata.note: A stored field id that is not a slug gets no class rather than an escaped one, and a catalog row with such an id is no row.

metadata.name: catalog-not-a-list
metadata.note: A hand-authored catalog of the wrong shape is no catalog at all.

metadata.name: row-of-unknown-kind-dropped
metadata.note: A row whose kind the renderers do not know is not a row: the field is treated as missing from the catalog.

metadata.name: text-value-not-a-string
metadata.note: The server always emits strings for text rows; anything else is an absent value.

metadata.name: whitespace-trimmed
metadata.note: Whitespace around a stored field, a title, a value or a placeholder is forgiven.
